claim.why_it_matters: The PDF prints this as a numbered section heading (bold, own line), like 6.4.2.2 on page 109 which the markdown renders as '###'; here it is left as a plain paragraph, so the section is invisible to heading-based navigation and section lookup.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 110 (II-26) prints '6.5 INTRA-PROGRAM COMMUNICATION' on its own line in the same monospaced typewriter face as the body text. It is not bold, so the claim misdescribes the PDF. The markdown carries the same text, word for word and on its own line ('6.5 INTRA-PROGRAM COMMUNICATION', page-110.md line 17). The only difference is that the markdown has no '#' heading markup, and every other heading on this page is treated the same way (6.4.4, 6.5.1 and 6.5.2 are plain lines too). That is formatting or navigation markup, not content: no word of the standard is missing or changed. Under the verification rules, a difference that is only formatting and does not change meaning is rejected. If anything, the missing heading markup applies to the whole page, not to 6.5 alone.
